decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already replaces the expressive terminal with the shared restrained architectural treatment, removes the obsolete exclusivity fact, and preserves the accent's literal correspondence to the Hero V.

The existing MODIFY captures the terminal change but leaves a stale identity_role that still describes an exclusive expressive signature and incorrectly removes the approved geometry reference even though the client requires the established structure and slope to remain unchanged.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

After comparing the kerning studies together, I am definitely most attracted to Option 2 (Balanced Flow). It reads as one unified word but still retains the airiness and elegance we have been developing.

Before proceeding with the material treatments, I want to reconsider the terminal used by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

We devoted substantial time to perfecting the Hero V before the rest of the alphabet had been created. At that point, the Hero V had to express far more of the identity by itself. With the complete wordmark now assembled, I no longer think it needs to be so expressive or decorative.

I’m seeking a feeling of precision, assurance, and quiet elevation. I’d like to test a terminal that appears more deliberate and architectural—a restrained, controlled upward release instead of a flourish.

I’m attaching two references that start to convey the quality I mean. I do not want either one reproduced exactly, but their cleaner transitions and more restrained elevation appeal to me.

The established structure and slope of both the Hero V and second V should remain unchanged. Instead, please create a few interpretations that preserve that geometry while applying a consistently refined terminal to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

Thank you!

value_updates.terminal_style: a deliberate, architectural, restrained, and controlled upward release rather than an expressive or decorative flourish
value_updates.geometry_preservation_constraint: Preserve the established Hero V structure and slope while refining only the terminal.
value_updates.master_geometry_role: The Hero V remains the system foundation, but its terminal should use a restrained architectural treatment applied consistently to the Hero V, second V, and É accent rather than functioning as an exclusive expressive flourish.
value_updates.identity_role: The larger opening V remains the wordmark's central hero; its left-arm structural philosophy guides the remaining letters, while its terminal uses the same restrained architectural treatment as the second V and É accent.

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already records the restrained architectural terminal and preservation of the second V's established structure and slope.
The source changes only the shared terminal treatment and explicitly preserves the second V's established geometry; its height hierarchy remains valid unchanged.

Changing the shared terminal style does not alter the requirement that the É accent and Hero V peaks align on the same horizontal reference line.
The existing same-message MODIFY already narrows the permitted revision to the shared terminal treatment while preserving all other established geometry and relationships.
The terminal refinement does not change the shared-baseline relationship among the wordmark letterforms.
The same source selects Option 2 Balanced Flow, which is already recorded; the subsequent terminal reconsideration does not change that selected kerning.
The source postpones proceeding with material treatment but does not change which signature elements receive champagne gold.
Reconsidering terminal geometry before continuing material work does not revoke or modify the selected Satin Reflection finish.
The terminal refinement has no effect on the all-caps wordmark treatment.
